findings.summary: Synthetic panel split: 15 tied to SoHo (5 live, 10 work), 14 to the Upper East Side (12 live, 2 work), 1 neither.

20 of 30 eat Indian food from a restaurant at least once a month (6 three or more times); 9 less than monthly, 1 never. By neighborhood, at least monthly: 11 of 15 SoHo personas vs 8 of 14 Upper East Side personas.
Most expect $15-$34 for a main (19 of 30); 9 expect $35 or more. By neighborhood, $35 or more: 6 of 14 Upper East Side personas vs 2 of 15 SoHo personas; under $25: 4 of 14 vs 7 of 15.

Satisfaction with current nearby Indian options is mixed: 13 of 30 satisfied (4-5), 9 dissatisfied (1-2), 8 neutral, 0 unsure. By neighborhood, dissatisfied: 6 of 15 SoHo personas vs 3 of 14 Upper East Side personas; satisfied: 5 of 15 vs 7 of 14.

Most common themes (respondents mentioning): consistent quality 24, better delivery and convenience 22, pricing and value 21, lunch specials and combos 16, authenticity and regional dishes 14, healthier options 10, transparent pricing and spice levels 10, ambiance and modern experience 9.
quotes: I'd eat it more often if there were a nearby place that felt genuinely regional rather than generic, with better spicing, fresher breads, and more thoughtful service. I'm also more likely to go if friends or a critic I trust recommends it.

I'd probably eat it more often if there were a few really good lunch specials or delivery deals under $15, especially something quick and flavorful near work. More variety and clearer vegetarian options would also make me try it more.

If the food were consistently good, reasonably priced, and not too spicy unless I asked for it, I'd order more often. I'd also be more likely to go if the menu was simple, the restaurant was reliable, and there was easy phone ordering with clear total costs.
More reliable delivery times, clearer ratings, and a few really standout spots with consistent flavor and service would make me order Indian more often.

caveats: Flashpoint synthetic panel: 30 AI-generated personas, not real people. Treat results as directional only.
Panel gender was matched to a US adult split; age, race, education and income were invented by the generator, not sampled from Census data.
Uncalibrated run (calibration_version=uncalibrated); persona answers generated by gpt-5.4-mini.
Neighborhood groups are tiny (SoHo n=15: 5 residents, 10 workers; Upper East Side n=14: 12 residents, 2 workers) and mix residents with workers differently, so comparisons should not be generalised.
Q5 theme counts come from Flashpoint's open-end analysis, which could not be filtered to this run; its base (30) matches this run.
Stated frequency, price and satisfaction are not observed spending; rents, competition and concept were not studied.
